gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each shortlisted camera costs once you add the part its parking mode needs, priced on the maker's own store today: Thinkware U3000 PRO Front & Rear is $549.99 with an OBD-II power cable in the box; VIOFO A329S 2CH is $459.99 + $25.99 HK6 = $485.98; A229 Pro 2CH is $349.99 + $17.99 HK4 = $367.98; A229 Plus 2CH is $229.99 + $17.99 = $247.98; Vantrue N5S needs a separate Vantrue kit ($29.99–$34.99). Also, of all of them, only the Botslab G980H 4-camera has cameras pointed out the side windows (120° each), but its parking mode also needs a kit that is not in the box.
standout_why: I compared against milewitness.com (cited; opened 2026-11-21). It names the A329S, U3000 PRO, BlackVue DR770X II, N4 Pro S, ROVE R2-4K DUAL and A229 Pro, and it gives pre-event seconds and kit names. But it prints no prices at all, never adds up camera plus kit, and does not discuss side or door coverage. I could not open vortexradar.com (HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and curl) or caranddriver.com (fetch blocked), so I cannot rule out that either one prices a kit. ChatGPT's own answer flags side hits as a limit but names no camera with side-window cameras. The standout drops to 1 if the Vortex or Car and Driver pages turn out to price kits.
decides: This confirms the Thinkware U3000 PRO 2CH as the out-of-the-box radar pick: its $549.99 includes the OBD-II power cable and has built-in dual radar. But the real gap to the VIOFO A329S 2CH shrinks to $64.01 ($549.99 vs $485.98 with the HK6 the A329S needs for hybrid parking and voltage cut-off). The A229 Pro plus HK4 ($367.98) is the value buy, with 15 s of buffered pre-event recording. For door and side hits, our Botslab G980H 4-camera is the only candidate with cameras aimed out the side windows, so it honestly wins that segment, with two caveats: its kit is sold separately and its page does not say which cameras record while parked. The Vantrue N5S's two extra cameras are cabin cameras (front cabin and rear cabin), not side-window cameras.
